# Issues and the board: gh dojo

This project tracks the issues of Trum-ok/gh-dojo on the GitHub Projects board of Trum-ok, project 5, with the process in `.github/dojo.toml` (preset `kanban`). Take, move, comment on, block and create issues **only** through `gh dojo`: never change a status, a comment, a blocked-by link or an issue with `gh issue`, `gh project` or the API. For what gh dojo cannot do, such as editing an issue's title, body, labels or assignees, use `gh issue` only when the task needs it or the user asks.

Start with `gh dojo describe`: the verbs, when to use each, what they need and do along the way, the lifecycle and the exit codes, read from the config without the network. `gh dojo <verb> --help` has the details of one verb. Read them rather than guess. When the setup is broken (token, board, config), `gh dojo doctor` names each problem with the command that fixes it.

A bare `12` or `#12` is an issue of `Trum-ok/gh-dojo`; an issue of any other repository is `owner/repo#12` or its URL, wherever a command takes an issue: verbs and their batches, `show`, `comment`, both sides of `block` and `unblock`, `--by` and `--blocked-by`. `gh dojo new --repo owner/repo` creates an issue in another repository of `board.repos`. The text names an issue of `Trum-ok/gh-dojo` `#12` and any other `owner/repo#12`; the JSON always writes `owner/repo#12`, and each issue has its `repo`. Free text in `--by` goes into the comment as is, so on an issue of another repository a `#12` in it links there.

## Lifecycle

`Backlog` → `In progress` → (`Waiting`) → `Ready` → `Done`, through `start`, `wait`, `ready`, `done`. A status in parentheses may be skipped. Each verb below says which statuses it moves from and to.

- `Backlog` is the initial status: `gh dojo new` puts new issues there, and an issue without a status or not on the board counts as `Backlog`.
- Final: `Done`. `gh dojo list` hides issues there unless `--all`.
- A blocker is resolved, no longer blocking, when it is closed or its board status is `Ready` or `Done`: its work is done though the issue may be open.
- A blocker whose status could not be read (`status not read: …`) counts as unresolved.

## Verbs

Run a verb as `gh dojo <verb> N` (`N`, `#N` or `owner/repo#N`); `--dry-run` prints its plan (status, links, the comment it would post) without changing anything. A verb adds the issue to the board if it is missing and refuses a closed issue unless noted. It confirms in one line, such as `#42 Backlog → In progress, comment left`: there is no need to read the issue again.

### `start`

**When:** you take an issue to work on

`gh dojo start N`: Backlog, Waiting, Ready → In progress; optional --comment; comments "Taken. Session: {session} {comment}".

- With an unresolved blocker it warns on stderr and still runs: read `gh dojo show N` and decide whether to take the issue, or ask the user.

### `wait`

**When:** work has stopped: waiting for another issue or an outside decision

`gh dojo wait N`: In progress → Waiting; needs --by or --comment; comments "Waiting for {by}. {comment}".

- `--by 12` (also `#12`, `owner/repo#12` or an issue's URL; several comma-separated, `--by 12,13`) also marks the issue blocked by #12. Text (`--by "the user's decision"`) only goes into the comment; issues mixed with text are an error (exit code 1); a pull request is named in the comment without a link. Once the blocker is resolved, go on with `start` or `ready`.

### `ready`

**When:** done, checked and committed to main

`gh dojo ready N`: In progress, Waiting → Ready; optional --comment; comments "{comment}".

- It comments only when given `--comment`.

### `done`

**When:** the change has shipped in a release

`gh dojo done N`: Ready → Done; optional --comment; also on closed issues; comments "{comment}"; closes as completed.

- It takes several numbers at once, `gh dojo done 12 13 14`: each issue is checked and written on its own, one that fails is skipped, and a summary names each issue not done. Running the same command again touches only what is left.
- For a release, `gh dojo release <tag> --verb done --dry-run` lists the issues the release includes (those the merged pull requests of its commits close, or its commit messages name after `close`, `closes`, `closed`, `fix`, `fixes`, `fixed`, `resolve`, `resolves`, `resolved`, `refs`), how each was found and its plan; without `--dry-run` it runs `done` on them as one batch. An open issue whose status it does not start from is listed as not ready and left out, not failed; only a later release whose commits name it again picks it up, so once it is ready run `gh dojo done N` on it. A closed issue it does not start from is refused (exit code 2): ask the user. The start is the previous version tag; the first release needs `--since <tag or commit>`. A number only commit messages name that is no issue (a pull request, a missing issue, or one of a repository outside `board.repos` not found or hidden from the token) is left out with a warning, not failed; `--exclude N` leaves out any issue found by mistake. In a commit message, put an example of an issue reference in backticks (`` `Fixes #12` ``): code does not count.
- It comments only when given `--comment`.
- An issue closed already stays closed as it is.

## Reading

- `gh dojo show N` before you work on an issue: its status, milestone, labels, blockers both ways (unresolved first, each with its board status), its parent and sub-issues (the same way), status history, description and the last 5 comments. `gh dojo show 12 13 --brief` prints three lines per issue, `--comments all` the whole thread (up to 100), `--full` everything uncut.
- `gh dojo next`: what to take next, the open issues in `Backlog` or without a status, with no unresolved blocker, in board order, 5 by default (`--limit N`). The blocked ones are hidden and counted; `--all` shows them with their blockers. Filters: `--mine`, `--label <label>`. Once you pick one, `gh dojo show N`, then `gh dojo start N`.
- `gh dojo list`: the open issues on the board, grouped by status; closed issues and final statuses are hidden and counted. Filters: `--status "<status>"`, `--status none`, `--mine`, `--label <label>`, `--all`, `--limit 100`.

## Creating and linking issues

- `gh dojo new "<title>" --type <bug|enhancement|documentation|dogfood> --body "…"`: the issue, its labels, the board in `Backlog`, in one command. A long body: `--body-file <file>`, or `--body-file -` for stdin. More labels: `--label X`. `--area X` adds the label `area:X`. `--milestone "<title>"`: an open milestone (an unknown one is exit code 1 with the list). `--blocked-by 12`: blocked from the start (repeat it, or comma-separate; an issue that does not exist is exit code 3, and nothing is created). `--parent 12`: a sub-issue of #12 (one issue; one that does not exist is exit code 3, and nothing is created). A title starting with `-` goes after `--`, and every flag before it: `gh dojo new --type bug -- "-v is ignored"`.
- `gh dojo comment N "text"`, or `gh dojo comment N --body-file -`: a comment without changing the status.
- `gh dojo block N --by M` marks N blocked by M without changing the status; `gh dojo unblock N --by M` removes that. `--by` repeats or takes a comma-separated list; another repository's issue is `owner/repo#12` or its URL. A link already there (or already gone) is not an error: the line says `already`. A pull request cannot block (exit code 3), nor can an issue N blocks (a cycle, exit code 1).
- An existing issue becomes a sub-issue with `gh issue edit N --parent M` (`--remove-parent` undoes it): gh-dojo has no command for it, since the link changes no status.

## Repeats are safe

Run the same command again after an error: a verb does not set a status that is already set, nor post a comment that is already the latest from gh-dojo; `comment` does not post its last comment again; `block` and `unblock` skip links that are already as asked; `new` with the same title finishes the issue it created instead of creating another.

## Session

`{session}` in a comment is a link to your agent session, from `CLAUDE_CODE_HOST_SESSION_ID` (the first one set). When none is set the verb warns and still runs.

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning | What to do |
|------|---------|------------|
| 0 | everything applied | go on |
| 1 | bad arguments or config | fix them as the error says |
| 2 | a process check refused | don't work around it; ask the user |
| 3 | issue or board not found | check the number (gh dojo list) or board.owner/project in .github/dojo.toml |
| 4 | network, rate limit or auth | retry later, or gh auth refresh -s project |
| 5 | partially applied | re-run the same command; it finishes the rest |

On an error, read its `error:`, `allowed:` and `fix:` lines. Never work around exit code 2: do not move the status another way, ask the user. On 4 and 5, run the same command again (on 4, a bit later).

A verb on several issues exits 0 when all are done, 5 when some were written and running it again may finish the rest, else with the code of the failed ones (2 first, then 1, 4, 3).

## JSON

Every command takes `--json`, `--jq '<expression>'` and `--template`, as gh does; an error is then JSON too (`error` with `exit_code`, `message`, `allowed`, `fix`), with the same exit code. Use it to pick values out of the output; for everyday work the text is shorter.

```sh
gh dojo list --jq '.issues[] | select(.status == "Ready") | .number'
gh dojo show 42 --jq '.issues[0].blocked_by[] | select(.resolved | not) | .ref'
```

## Commands

| Command | What it does |
|---------|--------------|
| `gh dojo agent install` | Write a skill or AGENTS.md section for agents from the config |
| `gh dojo block` | Mark an issue blocked by other issues, without changing its status |
| `gh dojo comment` | Comment on an issue without changing its status |
| `gh dojo describe` | Learn this project's process: verbs, statuses and exit codes in a few lines |
| `gh dojo doctor` | Find what is broken in the setup: config, token scope, board, repositories |
| `gh dojo init` | Write .github/dojo.toml for a board and check it against the board |
| `gh dojo list` | See what is on the board: one line per open issue, grouped by status |
| `gh dojo new` | Create an issue with labels, on the board, in the initial status |
| `gh dojo next` | Find issues to take: initial status, no unresolved blockers, in board order |
| `gh dojo release` | Apply a verb to the issues a release includes, found through pull requests and commits |
| `gh dojo show` | Read issues before working on them: board status, blockers, history, description, comments |
| `gh dojo unblock` | Remove blocked-by links of an issue, without changing its status |
| `gh dojo <verb>` | The verbs above: start, wait, ready, done |

# gh-dojo project notes

This section is the project's addition to the generated part above: the file `.github/dojo-notes.md` (`[agent] notes`
in `.github/dojo.toml`), inserted as is. Don't edit the skill itself: change the config or these notes and run
`make agent` (that is `go run ./cmd/gh-dojo agent install`; CI checks `agent install --check`).

## Process: which verb when

- `ready` only when the change is **in main** (merged, tests green), not when it is done on a branch. `done` starts
  only from `Ready` (`from = ["Ready"]` in the config).
- `done` only when the change has shipped in a release; **never without the user's word**.
- `done` for a release goes through `gh dojo release` once the tag `vX.Y.Z` is pushed: first
  `gh dojo release vX.Y.Z --verb done --dry-run`, show the list to the user, and only on their word run the same
  without `--dry-run` (optionally with `--comment "vX.Y.Z"`). Release finds issues by `Refs #N` and closing keywords
  in the commits since the previous version tag (`[release] keywords` in `.github/dojo.toml`); the first release takes
  `--since c720ec9`.
- A line `not ready (done starts only from Ready): #41 (In progress)` in release's output is normal: the release
  includes a partial commit (`Refs #41`) of an open issue still in progress. Release leaves it alone and doesn't count
  it as a failure (exit code 0). Don't move it by hand for the release. But it won't reach `Done` on its own: only a
  release whose commits name it again (`Refs #41`) picks it up; otherwise, once it is in `Ready` and shipped in a
  release, move it explicitly: `gh dojo done 41 --comment "vX.Y.Z"` (on the user's word, like any `done`).
- Exit code 2 from release is a refusal, not "not ready": for example, the issue is closed (`Fixes #12` in a commit)
  but not in `Ready` (`#12 is closed but in In progress`). Release won't move it now or later; ask the user.
- An example reference in a commit message (syntax, another repository) goes **in backticks**: `` `Fixes #12` ``,
  `` `refs: #12, acme/api#3` ``. Release ignores code; without backticks it takes those numbers as the release's
  issues. A real reference goes without backticks: `Refs #51`.
- A release warning like `acme/api#3: repository acme/api not found, or the token cannot see it: left out` or
  `#99 not found: left out` means the number appears only in a commit's text and there is no such issue (or the token
  can't see it); release skips it (exit code 0). If it is a false match, do nothing (or `--exclude acme/api#3`); if the
  issue is real but the token can't see it, tell the user. Only repositories outside `board.repos` are skipped: our own
  repository "not found" fails the batch (exit code 3), almost certainly because the token lacks access; tell the user.
- In `--comment` for `ready` and `done` it helps to give the commit or release: `--comment "5fc0e30"`.

## Inconvenience → a `dogfood` issue

Any inconvenience while working with gh-dojo (an unclear error, an extra step, a missing flag, help that lies, having
to work around it with `gh`): open an issue **right away**, without putting it off or quietly fixing it:

```sh
gh dojo new --type dogfood --body "What I did: … What I expected: … What I got: …" -- "<what is inconvenient, briefly>"
```

Then go on with the main task.

## What gh-dojo lacks

Here `gh` is allowed, but only when the task needs it or the user asks:

- close an issue other than through `done` (not needed, a duplicate) or reopen one:
  `gh issue close N --reason "not planned"` / `gh issue reopen N`, only on the user's decision (our config has no
  `drop` or `revive` verbs);
- change the title, body, labels or assignees of an existing issue: `gh issue edit N …`.

## Which version runs

The installed `gh dojo` is the build of the last `make install` from main, not of the current branch: a broken branch
doesn't break issue tracking. New behavior from a branch won't appear in `gh dojo` until it is merged into main and
reinstalled. The command table above was produced by the build that generated the skill; the installed version may lag
behind it:

```sh
gh dojo --version   # git describe of the installed build
make install        # in a working copy on main, after the merge
```
